findings.text: The opening three paragraphs tell a newcomer what Athena is, what a study is, and that this page is a study of firstmate. A first-time visitor can say what they are looking at within a few lines.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: Someone who lands on the Athena site expects to learn about Athena. Most of the page is about a different project, firstmate. Athena gets two sentences and is then only a demonstration, so a reader who came for Athena learns little about using it.
findings.source: Title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: There is a clear next step, but it sits near the bottom, after the long transition cards, glossary and limits. Nothing near the top points to it, so a newcomer who stops reading early leaves without a call to action.
findings.source: Next steps: "Learn about Athena, and how to install and try it: https://github.com/doodla/athena"

findings.text: The "Start here" section is a good on-ramp. It defines terms before using them and follows one task from start to finish in plain steps.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."

findings.text: The page says plainly what firstmate is and why someone would use it: parallel agents that don't overwrite each other's files and don't need a person to start each one.
findings.source: What firstmate is: "Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents."

findings.text: "In scope" is used many times but never defined, not even in the Glossary. A newcomer can't tell what makes work in scope for an automatic merge.
findings.source: yolo: "on, firstmate merges green, in-scope work itself"

findings.text: A merge is shown as a transition that stays in the Ready state, while t4 handles reaching Done. A newcomer may find it confusing that merging doesn't change the state.
findings.source: t10 ready → ready: "With yolo on, firstmate merges green, in-scope work itself"

findings.text: This sentence is awkward and hard to follow. Some trigger lines also mix deciders, e.g. t4's trigger includes "the merge lands" yet says "(decided by agent)".
findings.source: Transitions lead-in: "The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading."

findings.text: The limits section is honest that nothing was run. However, f2 and f3 explain the study's internal data model, which means little to a newcomer.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f2: "The study's data format asks every guard to name who checks it, and it has no way to say nobody does"

findings.text: Each statement links to its claim, and each claim to source lines at the pinned commit, which backs up the page's promise of traceability. On some list items the citation runs are long enough to make reading harder.
findings.source: Each statement ends with bracketed ids, e.g. "[c1] [c11] [c21] [c22]"
